title.narrative: Fostering Youth's Role in Community Developmen

description.narrative:
the action by the Hashemite University as a lead applicant and the King Husseing Foundation (KHF) as co-applicant through its community development Institute (CDI) will enhance the role of youth as co-actors in local community development to respond to community needs surrounding the Hashemite University in Zarqa and Mafraq governorates. To achieve the specific objective of the action in contributing to the improvement of youth's participation in the labour market and to foster youth's role in the development of their local communities, the action will 1) enrich the role of the HAshemite University's community service center to act as a hub for fostering youth civic engagement, and 2) strengthen youth capacities to implement community-responsive initiatives that serve the surrounding communities of the HAshemite university. Moreover, the youth through practical application of artificial intelligence in the design of their community initiatives will be better prepared for the labor market.

The action seeks to address the low youth participation in local community development. It will not only provide youth with comprehensive technical and professional capacity building but also will facilitate consultation and dialogue with the local community members and stakeholders, enabling benificiaries to become informed "rights-holders", empowering youth to take initiative, and to hold local "duty-bearers"accountable to community needs and obligations. The youth, in consultation with public, private and CSOs partners will assess and gather the actual needs of their respective communities to implement responsive community initiatives. The HU community service center hub will be established to become an agent for civic engagement, sustainable innovation from which the youth shall set forth on their civic engagement activities.

The target group will include 100 students of the Hashemite University (50% women, 5% PWDs). It also includes 6 Hashemite University Community Service ccenter staff and 20 partner members from the local communities affiliated with community-based organizations or the private sector.
